---
title: "Readings — Spatial libraries"
---

Every method in this unit is a way of asking one question: how does position survive the
trip into a sequencing library? Read each paper for that, and for the paragraph on tissue
preparation, which is usually in the methods and usually decides everything.

## Array capture

**Ståhl PL, et al. (2016).** *Visualization and analysis of gene expression in tissue
sections by spatial transcriptomics.* Science 353:78–82.
[doi:10.1126/science.aaf2403](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaf2403) — **start here**

> The array that Visium grew from. Look at how the permeabilisation time was optimised and
> how the barcode is carried through reverse transcription.

**Salmén F, et al. (2018).** *Barcoded solid-phase RNA capture for Spatial Transcriptomics
profiling in mammalian tissue sections.* Nature Protocols 13:2501–2534.
[doi:10.1038/s41596-018-0045-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41596-018-0045-2)

> The protocol version, with the troubleshooting table. Read it as a list of ways
> permeabilisation and fixation fail.

**Rodriques SG, et al. (2019).** *Slide-seq: A scalable technology for measuring
genome-wide expression at high spatial resolution.* Science 363:1463–1467.
[doi:10.1126/science.aaw1219](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaw1219)

> Beads placed at random and decoded afterwards. Note what is sequenced twice.

**Chen A, et al. (2022).** *Spatiotemporal transcriptomic atlas of mouse organogenesis
using DNA nanoball-patterned arrays.* Cell 185:1777–1792.
[doi:10.1016/j.cell.2022.04.003](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2022.04.003)

> Stereo-seq: the array is built and decoded before the tissue arrives. The methods give the
> methanol and pepsin conditions.

## Barcoding in the tissue, regions and in situ reads

**Liu Y, et al. (2020).** *High-spatial-resolution multi-omics sequencing via deterministic
barcoding in tissue.* Cell 183:1665–1681.
[doi:10.1016/j.cell.2020.10.026](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2020.10.026) — **start here**

> DBiT-seq. The splint-ligation design in the supplementary oligo tables is worth working
> through base by base.

**Merritt CR, et al. (2020).** *Multiplex digital spatial profiling of proteins and RNA in
fixed tissue.* Nature Biotechnology 38:586–599.
[doi:10.1038/s41587-020-0472-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0472-9)

> GeoMx. Compare what a tag is here with what a cell barcode is in a droplet method.

**Lee JH, et al. (2014).** *Highly multiplexed subcellular RNA sequencing in situ.*
Science 343:1360–1363.
[doi:10.1126/science.1250212](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1250212)

> FISSEQ. The crosslinking step is the part to understand.

**Wang X, et al. (2018).** *Three-dimensional intact-tissue sequencing of single-cell
transcriptional states.* Science 361:eaat5691.
[doi:10.1126/science.aat5691](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat5691)

> STARmap. Compare targeted padlock probes with FISSEQ's random priming.

  [STARmap](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/starmap__10.1126+science.aat5691/starmap.html)
- The vendor user guide for the slide you are using: its tissue-optimisation section is the
  authority on permeabilisation times.
